dod_intent_evidence: DoD intent is unambiguous — SBIR section shows two Air Force Phase II awards (2022, $732,146 and 2023, $1,347,050) for the InstaJam ATAK plugin — but the pack fails the evidence-sufficiency gate.
score_evidence: Pack own-language word count is ~242, far under the ~500-word floor — the website section is empty (no crawlable site content) and the LinkedIn about is a single sentence: "Building mobile on-device jamming detection and localization software."
No jobs data, no news beyond aggregator listings; scoring absence of deployment language against two SBIR abstracts alone would be unsound

What little language exists actually points the other way — "InstaJam is an Android Team Awareness Kit (ATAK) plugin (TRL7)", "JTACs can customize their own frequency ranges that mirror their PACE plan", "leverage mesh networking technologies (such as MANET)" — TAK-native, PACE-aware and warfighter-framed, which would score LOW on disconnect if it were scored at all
what_they_do: A two-person team building an ATAK plugin that detects and localizes RF jamming and shares the picture across a mesh network, so every airman becomes a spectrum sensor.
